steps.text: Place beef in a slow cooker and cover with onion. Stir together 1 cup water, ketchup, Worcestershire, brown sugar, salt, paprika, and mustard in a medium bowl. Pour mixture over beef and onion.
Cover and cook on Low until meat is tender, 9 to 10 hours.
Mix remaining 1/4 cup water with flour in a small bowl to form a paste; stir into goulash. Cook on High until sauce thickens, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Hungarian Goulash with Ketchup
raw_recipe.description: A slow cooker version of the traditional paprika stewed beef with dry mustard and Worcestershire for added zip.

review.reviewBody:
Finally, a recipe for Hungarian goulash that IS Hungarian goulash. I see so many recipes that as good as they may be are NOT really goulash, This IS. 
Very easily adapted to your liking by adding more or less of something. But if you follow this exactly you will have authentic Hungarian Goulash

Like a few others suggested, I seasoned the beef with salt and pepper and lightly dredged it in flour. I then browned the meat in batches. I also used beef stock instead of water.
I was feeding a crowd so I made a quadruple batch spread between 2 crock pots. Instead of cooking on low, I cooked on high and they were ready in 6 hours. Everyone loved it!

We loved the flavor! I had ground beef in the freezer, so that is what I used. It wasn't pretty looking, but it did work. I used 1 lb. Hamburger and cut the ingredients in half. I did not brown the meat, I just put everything in the slow cooker as directed. For thickening the sauce I used mashed potato flakes. I started with 1 Tb. And waited 5 minutes, then stirred it well. I continued adding a little at a time until it reached the desired thickness. This is faster than the flour method, in my opinion. I served it over pierogies. We can't wait to try it with stew meat!

I thought this was very good and flavorful. I didn't have 8 - 10 hours , so I cooked on high for 2 hours and on low for 4. It worked well, the meat fell apart and the vegetables were cooked. The only thing I did differently was to add carrots and added beef broth instead of water. . This is a good classic recipe.

`Well worth the 10 hour cook time ! Changes made was I added a carrot, celery and mushrooms seasoned the meat with salt and pepper then browned it in a skillet with olive oil placed the meat in the cooker then soften up the onion in the skillet and deglazed with a splash or red wine, added some red pepper flakes as well. I did use beef broth in place of the water. I used a well trimmed chuck roast cut into cubes. Served over homemade spaetzle with a dash of sour cream and a fresh baked loaf of artisan bread which soaked up the sauce quite well. Will do it again.

Absolutely fabulous!!! Only thing I varied from the recipe was I cooked it in my Instant Pot for 30 minutes and browned the meat with the onions before adding the rest of the ingredients (only because that seems to be what all Instant Pot recipes call for). Also couldn’t find Hungarian Paprika so just used regular. Definitely on my make again list!!

This is outstanding goulash! And as many said previously, is very authentic. My family really enjoys this flavor much more than a traditional American Beef Stew, so I will make it again and again. My mom is Slovenijan and will love this. After the pandemic we currently are living in, I will make it for her in the fall or next winter. The only thing I did different in this recipe, which may have affected the flavor, is that I recently made some of my own vegetable broth and used that instead of water. I always like to replace broth with water in recipes if it makes sense and in this case it sounded really good to me. Also, since I didn't have worcestershire sauce in the house, as we use it a lot, I used a quick substitute of soy sauce, lemon juice, sugar and hot sauce. I would definitely use the worcestershire in the future. Thank you for sharing this, Rhonda!
Followed the recipe, but cooked it in the instant pot (meat/stew setting) and had super tender and delicious goulash in under an hour. Will definitely make this again.

I try a lot of recipes from websites and such. I seldom go back on and do a "rate and review" though. Mostly because of time and not remembering where the recipe was found necessarily. Anyway - this one warranted my returning to the sight and doin so. This recipe is nothing short of AMAZING. My husband and I really like this and I will DEFINITELY make this again. It is a keeper! I used some of the advice from other cooks as in: substituting beef broth/stock (no sodium) for the water; browned the roast cubes before putting in crock and added minced garlic and a bit of red pepper flake. I'm sure its fine as written but always look at other's helpful (usually) hints. I knew our tastebuds were inline with those hints I decided to incorporate. Try this! You will not be disappointed!

This is a good, hearty dish. Per other reviewers' suggestions, I increased the paprika (used Spanish paprika that I had) to 1 Tablespoon, and I left out the salt. The ketchup has plenty of salt in it. Otherwise, I followed the recipe as written. The dish could have used a bit more seasoning, but if it is too seasoned, my kids won't eat it. My kids ate this dish. It had just a bit of sweetness to it that they liked. I liked finding another good slow cooker recipe that uses beef chuck as I am getting tired of pot roasts. I was able to assemble this dish quickly in the morning before heading off to work and came home to a house that smelled wonderful. To make morning assembly even faster, cut your meat and onions, and prepare the sauce, the night before and leave them in the fridge until ready to mix together in the morning.
Very tasty. I made a few changes, I used beef broth for water, and prepared mustard. I needed to add extra thickening too.
Loved the recipe! I used chicken sausage instead of beef. Making it again with mild pork sausage. Enjoy!

My mother before she passed had left this recipe to my grandmother and I was able to get it from her, before she passed. They both made this for as long as I can remember. Its nostalgic and wonderful. Nice to know another family enjoyed it as well. Not sure where they got it, but it's fantastic! My recipe is for stove top, so not too much different. I came looking for slow cooker, because, well life happens and it's always moving fast. Thank you!!
The long cooking time on low made the beef, which was a cheap cut, very tender. The flavors reminded me of my mother’s Hungarian goulash. This is a very nice meal with little effort.

I grew up eating this as my dad is Hungarian. This recipe is almost accurate, however, if you want it authentic you need to use both Hungarian smoked paprika and hot Hungarian paprika, as authentic Hungarian food tends to have some bite to it. I would also leave the brown sugar out as the ketchup is already sweetened, only use it if you are using tomato sauce (plain, NOT spaghetti sauce).

I don't know what put the idea in my head, but I decided to make and eat Hungarian Goulash, which I'd never before in my life eaten. 

So I looked around the internet for recipes. There are plenty. I am usually all for authenticity, but when I saw that a really authentic Hungarian Goulash is more of a soup than a stew, I decided not to be authentic. I don't like most kinds of soup, and especially dislike tomato-based soup. So goodbye, authenticity.

I was drawn to this recipe because I already had most of the ingredients on hand, and because it's simple and doesn't require chopping anything except one onion. (I hate chopping, dicing, mincing, etc., although of course I do chop, dice, and mince when it's necessary.)

Then at that point, the small amount of paprika called for gave me pause. Almost every other Goulash recipe I looked at called for much more paprika, at least two tablespoons and sometimes 1/4 cup! I am usually a stickler for following a recipe exactly, but almost I decided to go ahead and use more paprika. Then I figured out that a smaller amount was called for most likely because the liquid called for is lower than the amount of liquid in most other recipes, so I decided against more paprika.

By the way, for those of you who are saying that you couldn't find or didn't have "sweet paprika", so you used "regular paprika", in the US at least, regular paprika IS sweet paprika. In the US, paprika is either sweet, hot, or smoked. But the sweet is labled jus
Did not like the flavor. Won't make again.
I have made this for years with the same ingredients except for the meat. I use sirloin because I cook the dish on my stovetop. It is faster, the meat is tender and it tastes great!
I have been making this recipe for years. My entire family loves it.
